newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Jan Hub natgas ends lower but holds $4/mmBtu.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Jan Hub natgas ends lower but holds $4/mmBtu.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures finished much lower Monday, pressured early by revised forecasts for milder-than-expected weather and softer cash prices, sources said.

After hitting a low of $4.05 early on technical selling, January settled 38.1 cents lower at $4.192 per million British units. February ended down 22.3 cents at $3.697, narrowing the discount to Jan to 49.5 cents.
"Cash was off, but I think we'll see above $4.00 for the expiration. It would be hard to see an (Jan) expiration below December's settlement at $3.901," one source said.
He added that the contract's ability to hold recent lows at $3.90 and $4.05 lends more support to the contract, which expires Tuesday at 1300 EST.

However, the weather forecast has been the underlying factor. Temperatures are forecast to turn cooler in parts of the Midwest Tuesday through Thursday, with the cold air quickly moving into the Northeast by late Wednesday. The severity of the coldness will likely determine the movement in the cash market.

The cash market continued to erode as the morning progressed, stretching its discount to futures. Gulf Coast gas prices fell into the $3.80s late, with most deals reported done in the $3.90s, down about 40 cents from Friday. Midcontinent prices were equally lower around $3.70, while New York city-gate prices were talked late in the $4.20s.
Technically, support in January was pegged at $4.05, then $3.90. Resistance was seen at $4.50, then $4.60, the contract high, and then $4.62.
NYMEX said an estimated 36,915 lots traded, as compared with Friday's revised tally of 50,563. Open interest for December 20 rose 2,846 to 166,882.
NYMEX January Alberta natgas settled nine cents lower at $1.76. NYMEX said an estimated 30 contracts traded.

Physical December prices at the AECO storage hub were significantly higher in the C$2.95-3.00 per gigajoule range, or mid-$2.30s per mmBtu range as bitterly cold weather arrived in Alberta. January prices were talked at C$2.29 and C$2.30.
NYMEX January Permian natgas settled untraded at $4.30, down 10 cents. Open interest for December 20 climbed three to 92.
December Permian physicals were talked in the $3.70s to about $3.80.
On the KCBT, January finished down 34.3 cents at $4.120. Open interest for December 20 fell 300 to 2,751. The East/West spread was at 7.2 cents (NYMEX premium).
